newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RATHORE IN LINE FOR TEST RECALL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RATHORE IN LINE FOR TEST RECALL.

text.p: Indian opener Vikram Rathore enhanced his claims to be recalled for the third and final test against South Africa, despite the touring team's match against Free State ending in a tame draw on Monday.
Rathore followed his first innings century by hitting exactly 50 as India, set 284 to win in a minimum of 59 overs, ended the third and last day on 185 for six after a disappointing effort.

It was the dismissal of Rathore which ended the match as a contest, the opener having made his runs from 78 balls and struck seven boundaries before he played on against a seaming ball from Bradley Player with the total 78.
Rathore was dropped for the second test in Cape Town, but now looks certain to return to the side in place of Raman for the final test in Johannesburg starting on Thursday.
With Saurav Ganguly (1) and Pankaj Dharmani (11) both falling cheaply India were in trouble at 104 for four.
Their plight worsened when Rahul Dravid (44) drilled a catch to cover and Saba Karim got himself out to a long hop from Nicky Boje.
But Venkat Laxman held firm for 46 not out and a Free State win was never really on the cards despite men clustered around the bat.

Free State did their best to make a game of it in the morning. Resuming at 69 for no wicket, an overall lead of 93,Gerhardus Liebenberg and Deon Jordaan took their opening stand to 170 before Jordaan was run out for 66 made from 118 balls with nine fours.
Liebenberg went serenely on to his 13th first-class century, eventually hitting 133 not out before declaring. He hit 14 fours and a six from 176 balls in a high class display.
